messages.author: e5bf94f36294bdbd
messages.subject: Trying to obtain such plots "connectome + legend"
parts:
Hi all

I am learning R-language (mainly from the R-bloggers blog website) and
was wondering if such two figures

http://1.bp.blogspot.com/-f8As0iW3bL0/TzGD7vw5BbI/AAAAAAAACaY/VcvqKFD_oA0/s1600/connectome.JPG

http://2.bp.blogspot.com/-ju5ihQWivD8/TzIwiQntxFI/AAAAAAAACag/tK92-Jqv1i8/s1600/legend.JPG

are easily generated in R-language (although I want to learn how to
create them)

I can manage to get similar results using MATLAB but R seems such a
powerful tool when it comes to
data visualization that I would like to get comments / advices how to
get such customized graphs.

Thank you in advance for your time and help.

Best regards

Dr Brahim HAMADICHAREF

messages.author: 2710b717e5dbb066
messages.subject: Re: Trying to obtain such plots "connectome + legend"
parts:
I have seen something like the 1st graph done in R, but I don't
remember where. Adding colored rectangles based on polar coordinates
is fairly straight forward, might even be easier using ggplot2. The
connections could be made using xsplines. A lot of this depends on
what the data looks like to create the graph. I would not be
surprised if someone has already automated making similar graphs, but
you might need to tell us more about what field produces the data and
this type of graph for us to get a better idea where to suggest
looking (or to get the attention of others who do things like this).

The second graph could be done using pie chart functions and color
gradients. The plotrix package has a function for putting multiple
pie charts into a single plot if that is important.

messages.author: e5bf94f36294bdbd
messages.subject: Re: Trying to obtain such plots "connectome + legend"
parts:
Hi,

Thank you all for the few pointers. I will try to work on this in my
own time/speed while learning about R.

The field of research is neuroscience,  these two graphs are based on
the following recent paper

Circular representation of human cortical networks for subject and
population-level connectomic visualization
Irimia A, Chambers MC, Torgerson CM, Van Horn JD
Neuroimage. 2012 January
http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1053811912001255

I guess such plot can be used for other analysis visualization.

The data are square matrices with information about the brain matter
(grey / white), brain region,
and indivdual brain area. The arrows connections are based on the
matrix value typically with
value from 0.0 to 1.0. There are some detailed explanations in the
paper about the coloring which
I hope R can deal with very efficiently. I can share the PDF by email.

Brahim
